chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The testimony of women is valid in the 'udhrat (absence of men or private matters) and in every defect that a man does not see.

key_terms.الْعُذْرَةِ: Private matters or absence of men

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of women considered valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the scope of female testimony, distinguishing it from the general rule requiring two women for one man. It specifically validates women's testimony in 'udhrat (private bodily matters) and defects imperceptible to men, reflecting the practical necessity of their specialized observation in domestic and medical contexts within Shia fiqh.
